## 固定收益市場主論點

9月25日美國公債止跌回穩，但各天期表現分歧。油價下跌、短端殖利率回落，暫時中斷本週的賣壓，最長天期債券卻仍承壓。彭博每日殖利率序列顯示，10年期殖利率下降3.7個基點至5.163%；30年期盤中一度觸及5.53%，每日數值仍上升1.5個基點至5.494%。市場重新期待荷姆茲海峽能達成協議，帶動布蘭特原油下跌2.14%至每桶$104.32，卻未消除投資人對通膨、政府融資及聯準會還須升息多少的疑慮。

經濟數據則顯示需求與通膨走勢並不一致。8月耐久財訂單整體表現優於市場共識，但扣除運輸設備後的增幅不如預期；9月消費者信心下滑，家庭通膨預期反而上升。美國投資級、高收益及強勢貨幣計價新興市場債券利差均明顯擴大。週五較短天期美債獲得喘息，信用市場卻沒有相應改善，再融資成本、工程合約與個別借款人的損失仍是不可忽視的風險。

## 通膨預期升溫，較短天期美債仍回穩

週五盤勢先受惠於能源壓力緩和，隨後長債需求又遭遇考驗。有關重開荷姆茲海峽、解除美國對伊朗港口封鎖的談判消息，帶動油價回落；之後傳出伊朗提出的方案也將重啟核談判，使布蘭特原油在美國交易時段維持每桶約$104。協議仍未談妥，但談判對週五油價的影響，已與前一天重新走高的走勢不同。

密西根大學消費者信心終值優於預期後，長天期美債仍走弱。30年期殖利率盤中最多上升5個基點至5.53%，創2004年以來新高，10年期也一度突破5.22%。RBC Capital Markets策略師Izaac Brook指出，附近缺乏可參照的技術價位，殖利率因此容易繼續向上漂移。當時較短天期殖利率已經下降，反映的是殖利率曲線形狀改變，而非所有天期公債再度全面遭到拋售。

每日數值顯示，2年期與5年期殖利率均下降7.2個基點，分別至4.854%及4.988%；2年與10年期利差擴大3.5個基點至30.9個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大8.7個基點至64.0個基點。交易員似乎正在解除部分先前押注曲線趨平的部位。紐約時間上午10時前不久，5年期與Ultra Bond期貨同時出現大宗交易，成交價格與買進前者、賣出後者的操作相符。SMBC的Monty Gandhi表示，短線投資人認為，短端定價已反映相當程度的緊縮。

即使週五反彈，全週的跌勢仍大多未能扭轉：10年期與30年期殖利率分別累計上升16.6與16.7個基點。10年期實質殖利率週五下降4.4個基點至2.824%，損益兩平通膨率卻上升0.7個基點至2.339%，顯示名目殖利率下降是由實質殖利率帶動，而非長期通膨補償回落。全週實質殖利率上升14.7個基點，損益兩平通膨率則上升1.9個基點。

密西根大學調查顯示，家庭對經濟更悲觀，同時預期物價漲得更快。9月消費者信心終值為48.1，雖高於共識47.6，卻低於前值51.7。消費者預期未來一年物價上漲4.6%，高於8月的4%；未來五至十年的年均通膨預期為3.4%，創5月以來最高。

美國人口普查局公布的8月耐久財訂單近乎持平，各類訂單表現卻有差異。新訂單減少$1億至$3,386億，優於市場預期的下降0.4%；7月增幅則由1.1%下修至0.9%。扣除運輸設備後，訂單增加0.3%，低於共識0.6%，也不及前期修正後的0.7%；扣除國防訂單後則增加0.1%。

運輸設備訂單減少$7億，降幅0.6%，至$1,141億，為四個月來第三度下滑。另一方面，彭博報導企業設備訂單增幅高於預期。企業投資基本面並未崩跌，但涵蓋範圍較廣的非運輸訂單，沒有出現經濟學家原先預期的加速。再加上家庭信心疲弱，難以將需求概括為全面轉強。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack週五指出，長端殖利率上升不只是能源問題。經濟成長較強、投資人預期經濟將持續穩健，以及聯準會可能採取的政策回應，都是推升殖利率的原因。她也提及政府支出與累積債務，指出財政部正與AI專案競逐資金。借款成本因此同時受到資金需求與市場預期的聯準會利率路徑影響；她並未提出新的升息次數或時點主張。

Apollo首席經濟學家Torsten Slok則聚焦柴油傳導通膨的管道。他認為柴油成本會進入貨運、零售配送及資料中心建設，即使核心物價指數直接排除能源，燃料漲價仍可能傳入核心商品與服務。截至週四，美國柴油價格今年已上漲83%至每加侖$6.50，相較之下汽油上漲59%。Slok認為，必要運輸需求使這項成本難以迴避，最終轉嫁將限制聯準會把衝擊視為暫時現象的空間。

相較其他市場，債券波動率仍異常偏高。以週五盤中水準計算，MOVE指數全週漲幅約29.69%，回到3月以來未見的水準；VIX則收在14.87，當日下降5.11%。標普500上漲0.51%，那斯達克100上漲0.42%，後者全週漲幅達3.25%。儘管融資成本急遽調整，獲利信心與油價下跌仍持續支撐股市。

較高殖利率也吸引新的機構買盤。Lombard Odier Investment Management透露，旗下多重資產委託組合已在9月稍早動用現金買進10年期美債期貨，將美債配置調整為超配2%，這是至少五年來首次超配美債。總體研究主管Florian Ielpo預期聯準會只會再升息一次，認為美債殖利率對比美股盈餘殖利率已具有競爭力。他的判斷以中東緊張情勢緩和、科技業借款趨於穩定為條件，並不預期殖利率會迅速回到疫情前水準。

## 日本力挺日圓，各國緊縮壓力擴大

日本公布新的通膨數據之際，官員也協力釐清外界對政策立場的認知。日本央行扣除生鮮食品與特殊因素後的物價指標，8月年增2.6%，較7月的2.3%加速；排除項目更多、扣除非生鮮食品、能源與特殊因素的指標，則由1.6%升至1.8%。政府公布的物價指標顯示通膨低於央行目標，但排除汽油及公用事業補貼等因素的扭曲後，基礎通膨壓力更強。

這些數據強化了日本央行持續緊縮的理由，卻沒有消除內部分歧。Toichiro Asada與Ayano Sato上週反對升息時，都曾以通膨為由提出異議。隔夜指數交換定價顯示，截至12月再升息的機率超過90%；相較之下，9月會議前接受調查的經濟學家，最普遍預期的下一次升息時點是1月。

財務大臣片山皋月週五表示，川普在本週稍早與首相高市早苗會面時，曾對日圓疲弱表達關切，高市也認為日圓低估是個問題。稍後片山與美國財政部長貝森特通話，再次確認對日圓低估的關切；貝森特並公開支持強勢日圓，以反映日本經濟基本面。

經濟成長戰略擔當大臣城內實另表示，日本需要積極貨幣寬鬆與彈性財政支援來推升物價的時代已經結束，但他也指出，政府仍不認為日本已確定擺脫通縮。片山在訪談中則說，高市尊重日本央行獨立性，不應被視為主張再通膨政策的人士。她否認日本政策由美國壓力決定，並表示川普與高市未討論匯率方面的具體下一步措施。

日圓週五最多升值1.2%，至每美元156.94日圓。此番反應之前，市場看多部位已大幅縮減：美國商品期貨交易委員會週五公布的數據顯示，截至9月22日當週，槓桿投資人的日圓淨多單減少近80%，剩4,472口，約合¥559億。這反映在最新官員談話之前，日本央行升息並未為交易員的日圓看多立場提供多少持久支撐。

美元週五雖下跌，整體支撐仍在。美元指數當日下跌0.32%至100.97，全週仍上漲0.75%。摩根士丹利David Adams及其團隊週五撤回下半年美元走弱的預測，理由是美國成長較強、利差擴大，改估美元將維持強勢至年底並延續到2027年。宏利的Nathan Thooft則提出限制條件：市場已反映聯準會大幅緊縮，若通膨、就業或成長降溫，美元進一步上漲的空間可能較小。

英國央行總裁貝利週五表示，油氣價格居高不下的時間越久，就越難反對升息；若等到第二輪通膨效應有完整證據才行動，就會太遲。不過，他形容迄今成本轉嫁仍然溫和。這使他的立場更接近已朝緊縮傾斜的副總裁們，但他並未認為企業已全面透過調薪與調價作出反應。

英國央行先前以6比3維持利率在3.75%。若貝利與副總裁們轉向，就足以改變多數決結果。家庭能源帳單尤其棘手，預計1月價格上限重設時將提高約四分之一。勞動需求疲弱可能抑制薪資談判，但2027年薪酬協議的明確證據，要等到今年稍晚才會出現。

另一則報導指出，銀行正利用英國央行短期附買回融資操作，為持有英國公債籌資。本週透過該工具借入的資金接近£1,290億，但不能據此認定有多少流向這類交易。銀行可質押既有英國公債，以3.75%的政策利率借款，再持有殖利率較高的證券；10年期英國公債殖利率5.38%，便呈現扣除避險、資產負債表占用成本及價格風險之前的利息收益空間。

英國央行表示，這種用途獲得允許，也符合正常流動性管理。TreasurySpring的Glen Stone指出，已有超過70家機構使用該操作。這項發展反映流動性供應方式正在轉變，從央行購債注入，轉為銀行按需取得準備金。不過，若政策利率上升或擔保品條件收緊，融資優勢都會縮小。

歐洲央行副總裁Boris Vujcic則指出，能源壓力迅速緩和的期待還有另一項限制。他週五在克里夫蘭表示，受損煉油產能在可預見的未來不太可能恢復原有水準，柴油將因而維持高價，並把成本傳導至其他產品。他認為殖利率曲線重新定價與這種持續性有關。這項判斷針對的是成品油供應，即使原油運輸改善，供應仍可能受限。

加拿大方面，宏利將原先年底前維持利率不變的預測，改為未來兩次會議均升息。策略師Dominique Lapointe指出，核心物價指標的月增率換算年率已連續兩個月接近3%。他表示，目前還不能把這股動能歸因於伊朗相關的供應鏈影響，但衝突拖得越久，第二輪效應風險就越高。宏利也認為，貿易損害過度集中在特定產業，而失業尚未全面上升，因此不足以壓過通膨風險。

## 再融資成本與回收價值拉開信用表現差距

週五美國投資級與高收益債券利差擴大之際，已有跡象顯示，美債殖利率上升正在影響發債決策。企業本週在美國債市發行約$330億，低於交易商預估的約$400億；週初部分借款人額外讓利約6個基點，認購訂單縮減，至少一家發行人週三暫緩發債。富國銀行的Maureen O'Connor表示，市場討論已轉向美債是否超賣，讓擇機融資的借款人有理由等待。

企業獲利與負債導向投資需求仍支撐投資人，但利率變動越來越難以消化。MassMutual的Kelly Kowalski認為，殖利率若持續偏高且波動劇烈，終將拖累經濟活動、利潤率與信用品質。Columbia Threadneedle的Tom Murphy則區分了較高收益的吸引力，與殖利率快速上升造成的不穩定。經換約調整的CDX投資級指數週五約為58個基點，高於8月底的約55個基點。

Prospect Capital擬議中的再融資，具體呈現了借款成本上升的幅度。這家業務發展公司正洽談發行$5億、5年期債券，殖利率約8%，將是2021年以來首次發行非投資級債券。資金將用於償還11月到期、利率3.364%的債務，部分也將用於降低循環融資餘額並充實流動性。Pareto Securities已於週四舉行投資人電話會議，最終定價尚未公布。

Prospect表示，按交易完成後的試算，加權平均債務融資成本可能最多提高0.5個百分點至約6.5%，但強調仍低於11%的放款收益率門檻。兩者之間的差額仍須吸收費用與信用損失。穆迪將擬發行債券評為Ba1，提及近期獲利表現，以及相較同業較高的風險。因此，這筆交易不只是較高基準利率下的融資考驗，也反映該公司的信用狀況。

Brightline則於週四正式在紐澤西州聲請美國破產法第11章保護，推進先前研議的重整。聲請文件所列資產與負債各為$10億至$100億；這家佛羅里達鐵路公司的整體債務約$55億。營運公司未納入聲請範圍，與進入法院重整程序的其他實體維持法律上的分隔，列車因此得以持續運行。

Assured Guaranty與其他金融利害關係人也已同意，在其他實體走出破產程序後，向營運業務提供$4.9億，其中$3.5億為次順位債務、$1.4億為新增優先順位債務。新資金的受償順位並不一致，是這項方案的重要區別。Brightline先前因收入不如預期而無法履行借款義務，不同債權人陣營也曾各自提出重整方案。

HelloFresh週四晚間下修營運預測後，股債週五大幅重新定價。2031年到期、規模€3.5億的債券，價格一度每€1面額下跌6.8歐分，創7月發行以來最大跌幅；截至法蘭克福時間上午11時30分，報價下跌4.8歐分至82.4歐分。股價最多下跌15%，與債券一同創下歷史新低。

這家食材包配送公司如今預估2026年營收下降9%至11%，原先預估為下降3%至6%；調整後EBITDA預估由€3.75億至€4.25億，下修為€3.5億至€3.7億。縮減行銷支出已傷及重要開學季的客戶開發。管理層預估第三季營收下降11%至12%，調整後EBITDA為€4,500萬至€5,500萬。距首次高收益債發行僅數月，營運即惡化，顯示本業創造現金的能力一旦減弱，即使剛完成融資，借款人也可能迅速受到衝擊。

商用不動產投資人在費城Centre Square面對的則是損失回收問題。法院上月批准這座雙塔建築群以$7,000萬出售，相較2019年估值$4.71億大幅縮水，預計未來幾週完成交割。該物業是一筆$3.68億商用不動產抵押貸款證券（CMBS）交易的擔保資產。扣除墊款、費用與其他債權後，策略師預估優先順位部位每$1可回收約44美分，另外七個較低順位分券將全數損失。

Pimco持有該交易面額約$5,800萬，約一半位於原始最高評等分券。彭博估計，若按上述回收水準分配，投資損失將超過$3,500萬。出租率從融資時約93%降至6月底的28%，使貸款除了面臨估值下跌，也失去大部分收益基礎。若AAA級分券蒙受損失，將是金融危機以來第三起此類CMBS事件；目前已有超過30筆原始最高評等的單一資產、單一借款人交易分券，價格低於每$1面額85美分。

AI建設債務方面，摩根士丹利Lindsay Tyler與Vishwas Patkar週五針對已公開的甲骨文不可抗力通知，進一步區分各類融資的合約風險。他們認為，仍有大量工程未完工、或租戶信用較弱的交易，應受影響最大；接近穩定營運，或完工風險有限的資產，應較能抵禦衝擊。

該行強調，在其看來，甲骨文並非企圖逃避債務義務。疑慮在於支撐工程貸款的租約承諾是否可靠，以及私人融資合約缺乏透明度；若另一家高信用品質租戶援引類似條款，意義將大於單一爭議。另外，日本監管機關正加強檢視銀行與壽險公司的AI資料中心曝險，相關風險也受到監理機關關注。

大宗商品交易商Radiant World的債權人爭議，則出現新的法院介入。新加坡高等法院應瑞穗銀行聲請，週四任命KPMG主管擔任臨時司法管理人。法官對涉嫌詐欺的行為提出疑慮，也質疑該公司宣稱持有的逾$10億客戶應收帳款是否可信。這些資產能否回收仍有爭議，重整程序的控制權則已因這項任命而改變。

## 主權借款調整供給與債務減免進程

印度10月至3月的聯邦借款規模大致維持原計畫，但提高長天期發行比重。週五宣布下半年度籌資額為₹7.9兆，約合$824億；3至5年期債券占比將由上半年的23.5%降至19%，30年期以上則由24.9%升至28%。全年總借款由₹16.09兆小幅下修為₹15.99兆，淨市場借款維持預算水準。

到期年限的調整，是為因應印度央行另行出售以短債為主的證券、回收流動性。經濟事務主管官員Anuradha Thakur明確表示，短天期占比下降與這些操作有關。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership的Abhishek Upadhyay指出，長端配置比重增加令人意外，但也為印度央行進一步出售短債留下空間。基準10年期殖利率在此前一個月已上升27個基點；市場仍在適應流動性減少與潛在緊縮，又將迎來創紀錄的下半年度供給。

印尼新任政策首長則處理國內融資工具彼此競爭的問題。央行總裁Destry Damayanti與財政部長Suahasil Nazara週四晚間首次共同召開記者會，表示正在協調明年的政府公債及央行證券發行。Damayanti指出，印尼央行SRBI證券的溢酬已下降，接近與政府標售相符的水準。目標是避免期限相近的短期工具出現過大殖利率差距，並使流動性分配與成本更為平順。

先前SRBI殖利率具吸引力，將銀行資金從公債吸走，同時回收流動性，推高政府融資成本。財政部也呼籲持有大量存款的公部門機構，不要過度要求銀行提供高利率。週五早盤，印尼盾下跌0.1%至每美元17,919印尼盾，5年期公債殖利率上升3個基點至6.99%，顯示這項協調承諾是在外部壓力持續之際提出。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin則警告，歐洲央行援助有其限度。他在週五播出的訪談中表示，法國不應期待央行解決融資問題，必須自行採取支出與赤字措施；即使要使用維護貨幣政策傳導的機制，也需要先有這些行動。法國10年期公債相對德國的利差週五約109個基點，Moulin認為利差過高主要源於國內財政困境。

今年法國赤字預計達GDP的5.4%，高於政府原先5%的目標。Jupiter的Ariel Bezalel透露，他已出售大部分法國企業債部位，並放空法國公債期貨，理由是公私部門債務同時偏高。國際清算銀行數據顯示，第一季兩者合計借款約為GDP的324%。他以希臘作比較，是指財政惡化的方向；法國仍是投資級發行人，可順利從市場取得融資，所處的歐元區制度架構也不同於希臘在2010年面對的情況。

塞內加爾總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye最新談話則聚焦債務減免時程。他希望在幾個月內完成重整，並取得國際貨幣基金董事會對$22億方案的批准。政府已要求確認，精簡後的共同框架能避免其他國家經歷的多年延宕。Faye表示，取得方案的優先性高於明年的地方選舉。倫敦時間週五上午9時45分，2031年到期美元債上漲0.10美分至50.96美分，為五天來首次上漲。

阿根廷雖有政治風險，仍吸引買盤。Vontobel與施羅德已增加曝險，ProMeritum在8月初沒有阿根廷信用部位，之後也開始建倉。美元債自7月底以來跌逾6%，殖利率約10%。ProMeritum的Fernando Gimenez與Janus Henderson的Thomas Haugaard認為，相較短期選舉疑慮，目前估值更具吸引力；Haugaard特別提到財政紀律的支撐、外匯存底累積與反對派分裂。

施羅德的Fernando Grisales也提及石油產業投資，以及總統米雷的民調出現趨穩跡象。這些評估與其立法挫敗、國會是否支持對美貿易協議的疑慮相互拉鋸。Portfolio Personal Inversiones數據顯示，第一季本地投資人持有流通美元債的近四分之一，使國內情緒對交易環境具有格外重要的影響。分歧在於跌勢是否已充分補償風險，而不是風險是否已經消失。

巴西在10月4日選舉前實際調整政策。財政部長Dario Durigan表示，總統魯拉週五發布網路博弈臨時禁令，效期120天，之後須經國會批准才能繼續。總統選情膠著之際，這項措施針對侵蝕家庭財務的活動，但批評者警告，賭博可能轉向非法業者。

相關信用數據顯示，問題不僅止於博弈。7月有82%的家庭負債，創商業聯合會調查序列最高；未償信用卡債中近10%已逾期至少90天，家庭近三分之一收入用於償債。Serasa Experian統計，拖欠債務的企業達創紀錄的920萬家，逾期債務共R$2,390億，主要集中在小型企業。Insper研究發現，開始下注者的違約可能性高出近20%，顯示博弈與信用壓力有關，但不是唯一原因。

巴西7月名目財政赤字接近GDP的10%，利息占赤字逾90%。政府強調預算缺口已縮小，並預測明年將有小幅初級盈餘；前央行總裁Arminio Fraga則警告可能陷入衰退。禁令處理了家庭損失的一個來源，卻未解決償債負擔、消費與財政可信度之間更廣泛的相互影響。

週末孟加拉揭露首次發行外幣主權債的計畫。總理顧問Tanvir Shahriar Ghani週六表示，政府希望在三個月內籌得$5億至$10億，預計由摩根大通主辦，仍須取得總理Tarique Rahman最終批准。他表示，歐洲會談後機構投資人興趣濃厚，但強調聯準會升息後，政府對定價相當敏感，目前尚未公布架構或最終借款成本。

## 天候風險影響放款與主權信用

週五發布的一項研究發現，不同類型的房貸機構，對野火風險的核貸與定價反應並不相同。上海紐約大學Tyler Haupert與杜蘭大學Jesse Keenan分析2018至2020年加州超過73萬件申貸資料，成果刊於《Journal of Planning Education and Research》。在野火高風險地區，傳統貸款機構的核貸勝算，比幾乎沒有風險的地區低約15%；控制借款人、貸款與社區特徵後，房貸利率也隨危險程度提高。

金融科技貸款機構的核貸勝算卻沒有相應明顯變化，條件相近的借款人在最高風險區甚至取得略低利率。不過，研究並未證明是野火風險本身使線上貸款機構降價。資料早於2025年洛杉磯大火，且無法涵蓋保險安排、專有授信流程或各機構的風險評估。傳統機構的在地授信人員可能掌握標準化線上流程遺漏的資訊，也可能是保險或證券化把曝險轉移給了其他承擔者。

Resources for the Future經濟學家Yanjun Liao認為，核心問題是風險最終落在屋主、保險公司、房利美或房地美等哪一方身上。Keenan表示，若線上授信日後收緊，可能影響屋主出售或再融資的能力，但研究並未確立這種轉變會發生。研究呈現的是融資可得性與定價的差異，而非量化的房貸損失預測。

墨西哥巨災債券則有較為具體的風險更新。颶風Polo週五清晨重新增強為5級，風速約每小時180英里；不過Twelve Securis預期，它將減弱並以2級強度在下加利福尼亞人口稀少地區登陸。該管理機構判斷，墨西哥$1.75億巨災債券觸發賠付的可能性不高。風暴強度本身不決定賠付，路徑與中心氣壓必須符合合約指定條件。

週末報導則介紹T. Rowe Price如何在$1,650億的新興市場債券與股票投資組合中，運用約翰霍普金斯大學的氣候分析。研究規劃始於兩年前，目前工具已涵蓋12個新興經濟體的氣溫、降雨、水文與農業。主權研究主管Aaron Gifford表示，公司正適度降低哥倫比亞部位，因為乾旱同時影響水力發電與農業產出，而該國央行緊縮幅度又不及公司分析師預期。

該機構也計畫將研究用於評估小型島國借款人在天然災害後可暫停償債的條款，把分析範圍從大宗商品價格預測，延伸至合約付款彈性的價值。T. Rowe的Samy Muaddi強調，既有財政或對外收支的脆弱性，可能與市場低估的天候風險相互作用。除了美國利率帶來的共同壓力，這也是須逐國評估的風險。

## 後續市場焦點

週五收盤後，近期能源前景再度改變。川普拒絕伊朗的荷姆茲海峽七日重開方案後，伊朗週末拒絕放寬提案；不過川普向Axios表示，預期未來一週會恢復談判，也說正在非常認真考慮禁止柴油出口。週一台北時間上午7時15分之前的亞洲早盤，布蘭特原油上漲約1.5%，標普500期貨下跌約0.2%。接下來要看重啟談判能否敲定可執行的條件，而非僅憑談判消息，又帶來一波短暫行情。

柴油出口禁令構想另有供給風險。摩根士丹利分析師警告，限制出口可能使國內柴油價格降到促使煉油廠減少原油加工的程度，連帶降低汽油產量，甚至推升汽油價格。海外柴油則會更昂貴，歐洲尤其容易受衝擊。這種可能性，須與Vujcic對煉油產能損失的警告，以及Slok對貨運成本傳入核心通膨的疑慮一併看待。

貝森特週日從另一角度挑戰緊縮主張，呼籲聯準會官員在AI生產力與鬆綁監管改善供給之際保持彈性。他把這項機會與1990年代科技擴張相比，並主張核心通膨一直溫和。這番話凸顯分歧：尚待實現的生產力提升，與家庭、企業已承受的物價壓力，應如何權衡。

9月30日將公布8月PCE、所得與支出，以及第二季GDP終值和回溯至2021年初的國民所得帳年度修正。共識預估核心PCE月增0.3%、年增3.4%，前值分別為0.2%與3.3%；整體PCE預估月增0.4%，支出與所得則分別增加0.8%與0.4%。除了最新單月數據是否超出預期，支出及PCE的修正與方法調整，也使其背後趨勢值得留意。

勞動數據將從9月29日JOLTS職缺、9月30日ADP就業，一路接到10月2日非農就業。職缺預估723萬個，前值727.1萬個；ADP預估增加7萬人，前值3.8萬人。非農預測則有差異：經濟日曆共識為增加10萬人、失業率4.2%，彭博週末調查報導則約為增加9萬人、失業率4.1%。兩種預測都意味新增就業將低於前期16.2萬人。10月1日ISM製造業指數預估54.8，支付價格指數預估72，將另行檢驗經濟活動擴張與投入成本之間的平衡。

澳洲9月29日決策預計將現金利率提高25個基點至4.6%，聲明與總裁Michele Bullock的記者會，將說明11月是否還需要升息。較強的通膨與GDP支持緊縮，但失業率上升、房市轉弱與家庭支出放緩，限制利率可升至多高。歐元區9月通膨將於10月2日公布，彭博調查預估整體通膨由3.2%升至3.7%，核心由2.4%升至2.5%，這是歐洲央行10月會議前最後一份實際通膨數據。

本週發行不如預期後，企業債供給將再考驗需求。交易商預估未來一週美國高評等債券發行約$500億。Paramount Skydance正力求完成約$520億收購融資，$75億貸款已於週四啟動，接下來預計發行約$310億投資級債券及$124億第二順位擔保債券。整體融資規模龐大，月底完成期限又將到來，使最終發行讓利格外重要。巴西選前財政數據與羅馬尼亞可能於10月2日接受的標普評等檢視，則是另外兩項主權考驗：前者關乎償債成本與財政收支，後者關乎目前評等位於投資級最低一級的借款人。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌帶動美債局部回穩，長債仍走弱、信用利差擴大
overall_summary.session_narrative:
市場重新期待荷姆茲海峽達成協議，帶動布蘭特原油週五下跌2.14%至每桶$104.32，美債隨之回穩，但各天期表現分歧。2年期與5年期殖利率各下降7.2個基點，10年期下降3.7個基點至5.163%；30年期盤中一度觸及5.53%，每日數值仍上升1.5個基點至5.494%。由於短端已反映相當程度的緊縮，部分投資人平倉，解除先前押注曲線趨平的部位。

經濟數據未能化解通膨疑慮。9月消費者信心雖優於預期，仍低於8月；未來一年通膨預期則由4%升至4.6%。耐久財訂單近乎持平、優於預期，但扣除運輸設備後的增幅不如預期。10年期名目殖利率的下降由實質殖利率帶動，通膨補償反而上升。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered unevenly on September 25 as cheaper oil and a retreat in short-term yields interrupted the week's selloff, but the longest bonds remained under pressure. The 10-year yield declined 3.7 basis points to 5.163% in Bloomberg's daily yield series, while the 30-year rose 1.5 basis points to 5.494% after reaching 5.53% during trading. Renewed hopes for an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz helped Brent fall 2.14% to $104.32 a barrel. They did not remove investors' concern about inflation, government financing or the amount of further Federal Reserve tightening.

The economic news gave that concern a more differentiated shape. August durable-goods orders held up better than the headline consensus, although growth excluding transportation disappointed. September consumer sentiment weakened, while households' inflation expectations increased. U.S. investment-grade, high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads all widened noticeably. Friday therefore brought relief at shorter Treasury maturities without a comparable improvement across credit, where refinancing costs, construction contracts and individual borrower losses remained consequential.

## Shorter Treasuries Recover as Inflation Expectations Rise

The session moved through an early easing of energy pressure and another test of long-bond demand. Reports of negotiations over reopening Hormuz and lifting the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports supported oil's retreat. A subsequent account of an Iranian proposal that would also revive nuclear talks helped Brent trade around $104 during the U.S. session. These were negotiations over an unresolved agreement, but their effect on Friday's oil price contrasted with the renewed increase a day earlier.

Long Treasuries nevertheless weakened after the University of Michigan's final consumer-sentiment reading exceeded expectations. The 30-year yield rose as much as 5 basis points to 5.53%, its highest since 2004, and the 10-year traded above 5.22%. RBC Capital Markets strategist Izaac Brook said the lack of nearby technical reference points left yields vulnerable to further upward drift. Shorter yields were already moving lower, making this a change in the curve's shape rather than another uniform retreat from government debt.

By the daily observation, the two-year and five-year yields had each fallen 7.2 basis points, to 4.854% and 4.988%, respectively. The 2s10s spread widened 3.5 basis points to 30.9, while 2s30s widened 8.7 basis points to 64.0. Traders appeared to be unwinding some earlier flattening positions: simultaneous blocks in five-year and Ultra Bond futures shortly before 10 a.m. New York time were executed at prices consistent with buying the former and selling the latter. SMBC's Monty Gandhi said short-term investors judged the front end already priced a substantial amount of tightening.

The recovery left much of the week's damage intact. The 10-year yield was still up 16.6 basis points over the week and the 30-year up 16.7. At 10 years, the real yield fell 4.4 basis points Friday to 2.824%, while the breakeven increased 0.7 basis point to 2.339%. Lower real yields, rather than falling long-term inflation compensation, accounted for the nominal benchmark's decline. Over the week, the real yield had risen 14.7 basis points, compared with a 1.9-basis-point increase in the breakeven.

Michigan's survey captured the household strain behind the inflation debate. Final September sentiment was 48.1, better than the 47.6 consensus but down from 51.7 previously. Consumers expected prices to rise 4.6% over the next year, up from 4% in August, and expected annual inflation of 3.4% over the next five to 10 years, the highest since May. The better-than-expected sentiment headline was therefore not an improvement in confidence over the month. Households were more pessimistic about the economy while anticipating faster price increases.

The Census Bureau's August durable-goods release showed a less uniform picture than its flat headline suggested. New orders declined $0.1 billion to $338.6 billion, effectively unchanged against expectations of a 0.4% fall. July growth was revised to 0.9% from 1.1%. Excluding transportation, orders increased 0.3%, below the 0.6% consensus and a revised 0.7% rise previously. Orders excluding defense increased 0.1%.

Transportation equipment fell $0.7 billion, or 0.6%, to $114.1 billion, its third decline in four months. Separately, Bloomberg reported that orders for business equipment increased more than projected. The combination preserves an important distinction: underlying business investment was not collapsing, but the broader ex-transport measure did not deliver the acceleration economists had expected. Together with weak household confidence, the release made a blanket description of uniformly strengthening demand harder to sustain.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack identified several sources of higher long yields in remarks Friday. Stronger growth and expectations of continued economic performance were one; the prospective Fed response was another. She also pointed to government spending and accumulated debt, with the Treasury competing for funding against AI projects. Unlike a simple energy explanation, her account linked borrowing costs to both the demand for capital and the interest-rate path investors expected the Fed to deliver. She did not specify a new preferred number or timing of increases.

Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok focused on a more specific inflation channel. Diesel's cost enters freight, retail distribution and data-center construction, he argued, allowing fuel inflation to migrate into core goods and services even though core indices exclude energy directly. U.S. diesel prices had risen 83% this year through Thursday to $6.50 a gallon, against a 59% increase in gasoline. In Slok's assessment, essential shipping demand makes that cost difficult to avoid, and eventual pass-through would limit the Fed's ability to treat the shock as temporary.

Bond volatility remained unusually elevated relative to other markets. During Friday's trading, the MOVE index was heading for a weekly increase of about 29.69%, with readings back around levels last seen in March. The VIX, by contrast, finished at 14.87, down 5.11% on the day. The S&P 500 gained 0.51% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.42%, leaving the latter up 3.25% for the week. Earnings confidence and cheaper oil continued to support equities despite the abrupt adjustment in financing costs.

Higher yields also drew a new institutional buyer. Lombard Odier Investment Management disclosed that its multi-asset mandates had moved to a 2% Treasury overweight earlier in September, their first overweight in at least five years, using cash to buy 10-year futures. Macro research head Florian Ielpo expected only one further Fed increase and argued that Treasury yields had become competitive with U.S. equity earnings yields. His case depended on easing Middle East tensions and stabilization in technology borrowing; he did not expect a rapid return to pre-pandemic yields.

## Japan Defends the Yen as Policy Pressure Broadens

Japan supplied a fresh inflation observation alongside a coordinated effort to change perceptions of its policy stance. The BOJ's measure excluding fresh food and special factors rose 2.6% in August from a year earlier, accelerating from 2.3% in July. A narrower measure excluding non-fresh food, energy and special factors increased to 1.8% from 1.6%. Removing distortions such as gasoline and utility subsidies revealed greater underlying pressure than government measures showing inflation below the central bank's target.

That evidence matters to the disagreement within the BOJ. Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato had opposed the previous week's increase, citing inflation in their dissents. Friday's release strengthened the case for continued tightening without eliminating that division. Overnight index swaps implied more than a 90% chance of another increase by December, while the economists surveyed before the September meeting had most commonly expected the next move in January.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Friday that Donald Trump had expressed concern about yen weakness in his meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi earlier in the week, and that Takaichi had also described an undervalued yen as problematic. Later, Katayama and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke by telephone and reaffirmed concern about the currency's undervaluation. Bessent publicly endorsed a strong yen reflecting Japan's economic fundamentals.

Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi separately said the era requiring aggressive monetary easing and flexible fiscal support to reflate Japan was over. His qualification was important: the government still did not regard the country as having definitively escaped deflation. Katayama, in an interview, said Takaichi respected BOJ independence and should not be characterized as a reflationist. She denied that U.S. pressure was determining Japanese policy and said Trump and Takaichi had not discussed specific next steps on the currency.

The yen strengthened as much as 1.2% to 156.94 per dollar Friday. The response followed a substantial reduction in bullish positioning: CFTC figures released Friday showed leveraged investors' net yen longs had fallen nearly 80% in the week ended September 22, to 4,472 contracts, or about JPY55.9 billion. That earlier positioning retreat showed how little lasting support traders had taken from the BOJ's rate increase before the latest official comments.

The dollar's broader backdrop remained firm despite its Friday decline. The Dollar Index fell 0.32% to 100.97 for the session but was up 0.75% over the week. Morgan Stanley's David Adams and colleagues abandoned their forecast for second-half dollar weakness on Friday, citing stronger U.S. growth and wider interest differentials, and now expected strength through year-end and into 2027. Manulife's Nathan Thooft offered a restraint on that view: substantial Fed tightening was already priced, so cooling inflation, employment or growth could leave less room for further dollar gains.

In Britain, Governor Andrew Bailey brought his own judgment to the developing case for a BOE increase. He said Friday that resisting a rise would become harder the longer high oil and gas prices persisted, and that waiting for complete evidence of second-round inflation would leave the bank acting too late. At the same time, he described pass-through so far as subdued. His position narrowed the distance between the governor and deputies already moving toward tightening, without treating firms' wage and price responses as fully realized.

The BOE had held at 3.75% by a 6-3 vote. A shift by Bailey and his deputies would be sufficient to change that majority. The problem was particularly acute for prospective household energy bills, which were on course to rise by about a quarter at January's price-cap reset. Weak labor demand could restrain wage bargaining, but firm evidence on 2027 pay agreements would arrive only later in the year.

Separate reporting showed banks using the BOE's short-term repo facility to finance gilt holdings. Almost GBP129 billion was borrowed through the facility during the week, although that total does not establish how much financed this particular trade. Banks can pledge existing gilts, borrow at the 3.75% policy rate and hold securities yielding more; a 10-year gilt at 5.38% illustrated the available gross carry before hedging, balance-sheet charges and price risk.

The BOE said such use was permitted and consistent with normal liquidity management. More than 70 institutions had accessed the operation, according to TreasurySpring's Glen Stone. The development reflects the transition away from liquidity supplied through bond purchases toward banks obtaining reserves on demand. It also leaves the trade sensitive to a higher policy rate or tighter collateral terms, either of which would reduce its financing advantage.

ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic emphasized a different limitation on hopes for rapid energy relief. Speaking in Cleveland Friday, he said damaged refining capacity was unlikely to return to its earlier level in the foreseeable future, keeping diesel expensive and feeding costs into other products. He associated the repricing of yield curves with that persistence. His assessment concerns the availability of refined fuel, which could remain constrained even if crude shipping improves.

In Canada, Manulife changed its forecast from a hold through year-end to increases at the next two meetings. Strategist Dominique Lapointe cited core measures running near 3% on a monthly annualized basis for two consecutive months. He said that momentum could not yet be attributed to Iran-related supply chains, but the duration of the conflict increased the risk of second-round effects. The firm also judged trade damage too concentrated in particular industries to outweigh inflation risks for an economy that had avoided a broad rise in unemployment.

## Refinancing Costs and Recovery Values Divide Credit

Friday's wider U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads accompanied evidence that higher Treasury yields were affecting issuance decisions. Companies sold about $33 billion of U.S. bonds over the week, below dealers' roughly $40 billion forecast. Some borrowers paid about 6 basis points of additional concession earlier in the week, order books diminished and at least one issuer stood down Wednesday. Wells Fargo's Maureen O'Connor said the conversation had shifted toward whether the Treasury market was oversold, giving opportunistic borrowers a reason to wait.

Investors were still receiving support from earnings and liability-driven demand, but the change in rates was becoming harder to absorb. MassMutual's Kelly Kowalski argued that persistently high and volatile yields would eventually weigh on activity, margins and credit quality. Columbia Threadneedle's Tom Murphy distinguished the appeal of higher income from the destabilizing speed at which yields had risen. The roll-adjusted CDX investment-grade index was around 58 basis points Friday, compared with about 55 at August's end.

Prospect Capital's proposed refinancing put a concrete price on that pressure. The business development company was discussing an approximately 8% yield for a $500 million five-year bond, its first junk-bond offering since 2021. It would refinance debt carrying a 3.364% interest rate and maturing in November, with some proceeds also used to reduce its revolving facility and bolster liquidity. Pareto Securities had held investor calls Thursday; final pricing had not been announced.

Prospect said the transaction could raise its weighted-average debt-financing cost by as much as 0.5 percentage point to about 6.5% on a pro forma basis. The company emphasized that this remained below an 11% lending-yield threshold. The gap still has to accommodate fees and credit losses. Moody's assigned the proposed issue Ba1, citing recent earnings performance and a riskier profile than peers, making the transaction a test of both higher benchmark rates and the lender's own credit standing.

Brightline moved from a contemplated restructuring to a completed Chapter 11 filing Thursday in New Jersey. The petition listed assets and liabilities of $1 billion-$10 billion each, while excluding the operating company so trains could keep running. The Florida railroad's broader debt stack totals about $5.5 billion. Its operating-company exclusion preserves the legal separation around the service while other entities restructure under court protection.

The new funding package was also more definite. Assured Guaranty and other financial stakeholders agreed to provide the operating business with $490 million after the other entities emerge from bankruptcy: $350 million of junior debt and $140 million of additional senior debt. That composition matters alongside the filing itself, because the new money is not all entering at the same rank. Lower-than-expected revenue had left Brightline unable to meet its borrowing obligations, and competing creditor groups had previously put forward restructuring proposals.

HelloFresh experienced a sharp repricing after reducing its operating forecasts late Thursday. Its EUR350 million bond due in 2031 fell as much as 6.8 cents on the euro Friday, its largest decline since issuance in July. By 11:30 a.m. Frankfurt time it was quoted 4.8 cents lower at 82.4. The shares fell as much as 15%, reaching a record low along with the debt.

The meal-kit company now expects 2026 revenue to fall 9%-11%, against its previous 3%-6% decline, and adjusted EBITDA of EUR350 million-EUR370 million rather than EUR375 million-EUR425 million. Reduced marketing spending had hurt customer acquisition in the important back-to-school period. For Q3, management expects revenue down 11%-12% and adjusted EBITDA of EUR45 million-EUR55 million. The deterioration came only months after its debut high-yield offering and showed how quickly weaker operating cash generation could unsettle a newly financed borrower.

Commercial-property investors faced a different loss calculation at Philadelphia's Centre Square. A court approved the two-tower complex's $70 million sale last month, against a $471 million appraisal in 2019, with closing expected in the coming weeks. The property supports a $368 million CMBS transaction. After advances, fees and other claims, strategists expected recovery of about 44 cents on the dollar for the senior exposure, with seven lower-ranking tranches wiped out.

Pimco holds roughly $58 million face value across the transaction, about half in the originally top-rated portion. Bloomberg estimated investment losses exceeding $35 million at that recovery level. The figures are prospective distributions, not a completed payout. Occupancy had fallen from around 93% at the financing to 28% at June's end, leaving the loan exposed to a much smaller income base as well as lower valuation. A loss at the AAA level would be only the third such CMBS event since the financial crisis; more than 30 originally top-rated slices of single-asset, single-borrower deals were already trading below 85 cents.

AI construction debt acquired a new analytical distinction rather than another general warning about issuance. Morgan Stanley's Lindsay Tyler and Vishwas Patkar said Friday that Oracle's force majeure notice should have the greatest impact on transactions with substantial unfinished construction or weaker tenants. Assets approaching stabilization, or with limited completion risk, should be better insulated. The notice was already known; the fresh assessment identified which financings were most exposed to its contractual implications.

The bank said another high-quality tenant invoking similar provisions would be more significant than an isolated dispute. It also stressed that Oracle's action was not, in its view, an attempt to evade debt obligations. The concern is the reliability of lease commitments supporting construction loans and the limited visibility into privately financed contracts. Japanese regulators were separately increasing scrutiny of banks' and life insurers' AI data-center exposures, adding a supervisory dimension to that examination.

At commodity trader Radiant World, the creditor dispute produced a new court intervention. Singapore's High Court appointed KPMG executives as interim judicial managers Thursday on Mizuho Bank's application. The judge raised concerns about alleged fraudulent conduct and the credibility of more than $1 billion in claimed customer receivables. The appointment changes control of the restructuring process while the recoverability of those assets remains contested.

## Sovereigns Adjust Supply and Debt Relief

India kept its October-March federal borrowing near plan while shifting more issuance toward long maturities. Friday's announcement set second-half fundraising at INR7.9 trillion, about $82.4 billion. The share of three- to five-year bonds will fall to 19% from 23.5% in the first half, while securities maturing in 30 years or more rise to 28% from 24.9%. Full-year gross borrowing was trimmed to INR15.99 trillion from INR16.09 trillion, with net market borrowing unchanged at the budgeted level.

The maturity change responds to the RBI's separate liquidity-draining sales, which are concentrated in shorter paper. Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur explicitly linked the reduced short-maturity share to those operations. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership's Abhishek Upadhyay said the larger long-end allocation was a surprise but created room for further RBI sales at the short end. The benchmark 10-year yield had risen 27 basis points over the preceding month, leaving the record second-half supply to meet a market already adjusting to less liquidity and possible tightening.

Indonesia's new policy chiefs were addressing a related conflict between competing domestic instruments. Governor Destry Damayanti and Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said in their first joint briefing late Thursday that they were coordinating government-bond and central-bank security issuance for next year. Damayanti said premiums on the BOJ's Indonesian counterpart's SRBI securities had already declined toward levels consistent with government auctions. The aim was to avoid large yield gaps between similarly short-dated instruments and smooth the distribution and cost of liquidity.

Previously, attractive SRBI yields had drawn bank money away from government debt while absorbing liquidity, raising the state's financing cost. The finance ministry also urged public agencies with large deposits not to press banks too aggressively for high rates. Early Friday, the rupiah was down 0.1% at 17,919 per dollar and the five-year government yield was up 3 basis points at 6.99%, showing that the coordination pledge arrived amid continuing external pressure.

France's fiscal debate acquired a direct warning about the limits of ECB assistance. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said in an interview broadcast Friday that the country should not expect the central bank to resolve its financing problem. National spending and deficit measures were necessary, he said, including for access to mechanisms intended to protect monetary-policy transmission. The French 10-year premium over Germany was around 109 basis points Friday, and Moulin attributed the excessive spread principally to domestic fiscal difficulties.

The deficit is expected to reach 5.4% of output this year rather than the government's initial 5% objective. Jupiter's Ariel Bezalel disclosed that he had sold most French corporate holdings and was short French sovereign futures, citing the combination of private and public indebtedness. BIS figures put their combined borrowing at about 324% of GDP in Q1. His comparison with Greece concerned the direction of fiscal deterioration; France remains an investment-grade issuer with ready market access and a euro-area institutional framework different from the one confronting Greece in 2010.

Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye put the prospective timing of debt relief at the center of his latest comments. He said he hoped to complete the restructuring process and secure IMF board approval for a $2.2 billion program within months. The government had sought assurances that a streamlined Common Framework would avoid the multiyear delays experienced elsewhere. Faye said obtaining the program would take precedence over next year's local elections. The 2031 dollar bond added 0.10 cent to 50.96 cents at 9:45 a.m. London time Friday, its first rise in five days.

Argentina attracted buyers despite its political risk. Vontobel and Schroders had increased exposure, while ProMeritum built a position after entering August without Argentine credit. Dollar bonds had lost more than 6% since July's end and offered yields around 10%. ProMeritum's Fernando Gimenez and Janus Henderson's Thomas Haugaard judged valuations more compelling than the near-term election concern, with Haugaard pointing to the fiscal anchor, reserve accumulation and a fragmented opposition.

Schroders' Fernando Grisales also cited oil-sector investment and signs that President Javier Milei's polling was stabilizing. Those assessments run against legislative setbacks and doubts about congressional support for his U.S. trade agreement. Local investors held almost a quarter of outstanding dollar bonds in Q1, according to Portfolio Personal Inversiones, giving domestic sentiment an unusually important role in trading conditions. The disagreement was over whether the selloff already compensated for those risks, not whether they had disappeared.

Brazil supplied an actual policy change ahead of its October 4 election. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva issued a provisional ban on online gambling Friday, according to Finance Minister Dario Durigan. It applies for 120 days and then requires congressional approval to remain effective. The measure targets a drain on household finances in a close presidential contest, although critics warn activity could shift to illegal operators.

The associated credit data show a broader problem than gambling alone. In July, 82% of households carried debt, the highest share in the commerce confederation's series, while nearly 10% of outstanding credit-card debt was at least 90 days overdue. Families were allocating nearly one-third of income to debt service. Serasa Experian counted a record 9.2 million delinquent companies with BRL239 billion of overdue obligations, mostly at small businesses. An Insper study found people who began betting were nearly 20% more likely to default, connecting the targeted activity to credit stress without making it the sole cause.

Brazil's nominal fiscal deficit was nearly 10% of GDP in July, with interest accounting for more than 90% of the shortfall. The administration points to a narrower budget gap and forecasts a small primary surplus next year, while former central-bank governor Arminio Fraga warned of a possible recession. The ban addresses one source of household losses but leaves the larger interaction of debt service, consumption and fiscal credibility unresolved.

Over the weekend, Bangladesh disclosed plans for its first foreign-currency sovereign bond. Prime-ministerial adviser Tanvir Shahriar Ghani said Saturday that the government sought $500 million-$1 billion within three months, with JPMorgan expected to manage the sale. Final approval from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman remains necessary. Ghani reported strong institutional interest after European meetings but stressed sensitivity to pricing after the Fed's increase. No structure or final borrowing cost was announced.

## Weather Exposure Reaches Lending and Sovereign Risk

A study published Friday added new evidence on how mortgage origination channels price physical risk. Tyler Haupert of New York University Shanghai and Jesse Keenan of Tulane examined more than 730,000 California applications from 2018-2020 for research in the Journal of Planning Education and Research. In high-wildfire-risk neighborhoods, traditional lenders' approval odds were about 15% lower than in areas with essentially no risk. Their mortgage rates also increased with danger after accounting for borrower, loan and neighborhood characteristics.

Fintech lenders showed little corresponding change in approval odds, and comparable borrowers in the highest-risk areas received somewhat lower rates. The authors did not establish that wildfire risk itself caused online lenders to lower prices. Their data predate the 2025 Los Angeles fires and could not capture insurance arrangements, proprietary underwriting or each lender's risk assessment. Traditional local officers may have access to information that standardized online processes miss; alternatively, insurance or securitization may allocate the exposure elsewhere.

Resources for the Future economist Yanjun Liao said the key question was who ultimately carried the risk, including homeowners, insurers and Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. A later tightening of online underwriting could affect owners' ability to sell or refinance, Keenan said, but the study did not establish that such a shift would occur. Its contribution is an observed difference in credit access and pricing, not a measured mortgage-loss forecast.

Mexico's catastrophe-bond exposure received a narrower update. Hurricane Polo had regained Category 5 strength with winds around 180 miles an hour early Friday, yet Twelve Securis expected it to weaken and make landfall as a Category 2 storm in a sparsely populated part of Baja California. The manager judged activation of Mexico's $175 million bond unlikely. The storm's headline intensity alone does not determine payment: its path and central pressure must meet the contract's specified conditions.

Weekend reporting described T. Rowe Price's use of Johns Hopkins climate analytics across a $165 billion emerging-market debt and equity book. Research planning began two years ago, and the tools now cover temperature, rainfall, hydrology and agriculture in 12 emerging economies. Sovereign research director Aaron Gifford said the firm was moderating Colombian positions because drought affects both hydroelectricity and agricultural output, while the central bank had tightened less than its analysts expected.

The manager also intends to use the research when assessing clauses that let small island borrowers suspend debt payments after natural disasters. That extends the analysis beyond commodity-price forecasts into the value of contractual payment flexibility. T. Rowe's Samy Muaddi emphasized the intersection of existing fiscal or external weakness with weather risks markets may underestimate, a country-specific concern alongside the common pressure from U.S. rates.

## Forward Market Significance

The immediate energy outlook changed after Friday's close. Over the weekend, Iran refused to soften its seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal after Trump rejected it, although he told Axios he expected negotiations to resume during the coming week. He also said he was considering a diesel-export ban very seriously. In early Asian trading before Monday's 7:15 a.m. Taipei boundary, Brent rose about 1.5% and S&P 500 futures fell around 0.2%. The next test is whether renewed talks can produce operational terms, rather than another temporary repricing on their existence.

The diesel proposal carries a separate supply risk. Morgan Stanley analysts warned that restricting exports could reduce domestic diesel prices enough to encourage refiners to cut crude processing, lowering gasoline production and potentially raising gasoline prices. Overseas diesel would become more expensive, with Europe particularly exposed. That possibility matters alongside Vujcic's warning about lost refining capacity and Slok's concern about freight costs entering core inflation.

Bessent added a distinct weekend challenge to the tightening case, urging Fed officials Sunday to remain flexible as AI productivity and deregulation improve supply. He compared the opportunity with the 1990s technology expansion and argued that core inflation had been subdued. His comments set up a disagreement over the balance between prospective productivity gains and the price pressures already affecting households and businesses.

September 30 brings August PCE, income and spending, alongside final Q2 GDP and annual national-account revisions reaching back to early 2021. Consensus expects core PCE up 0.3% monthly and 3.4% annually, after 0.2% and 3.3%, with headline PCE up 0.4% on the month. Spending is expected to rise 0.8% and income 0.4%. Revisions and methodological changes to spending and PCE will make the underlying trajectory important as well as the latest monthly surprise.

The labor sequence runs from September 29 JOLTS through September 30 ADP to October 2 payrolls. Job openings are expected at 7.23 million versus 7.271 million, and ADP at 70,000 versus 38,000. Payroll forecasts differ: the economic-calendar consensus is 100,000 with 4.2% unemployment, while Bloomberg's weekend survey account points to about 90,000 and 4.1%. Either forecast implies slower hiring than the previous 162,000 increase. October 1 ISM manufacturing, expected at 54.8 with prices paid at 72, will separately test the balance between expanding activity and input costs.

Australia's September 29 decision is expected to lift the cash rate 25 basis points to 4.6%. The statement and Michele Bullock's press conference will address whether another increase in November is necessary. Stronger inflation and GDP have supported tightening, but rising unemployment, weaker housing and slowing household spending constrain how far rates can go. Euro-area September inflation follows October 2, with a Bloomberg survey expecting 3.7% headline inflation after 3.2% and core inflation at 2.5% after 2.4%, the last hard inflation release before the ECB's October meeting.

Corporate supply will test demand after the week's shortfall. Dealers expect about $50 billion of U.S. high-grade sales in the coming week. Paramount Skydance is seeking to complete roughly $52 billion of acquisition financing, with its $7.5 billion loan launched Thursday and approximately $31 billion of investment-grade bonds and $12.4 billion of second-lien bonds expected next. The larger package and approaching month-end completion deadline make final concessions important. Brazil's pre-election fiscal releases and Romania's potential October 2 S&P rating review pose separate sovereign tests: the former for debt-service arithmetic, the latter for a borrower at the lowest investment-grade rating.

overall_summary.headline: Cheaper oil brings uneven Treasury relief as long bonds weaken and credit spreads widen
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered unevenly on Friday as renewed hopes for an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz helped Brent fall 2.14% to $104.32 a barrel. The 2-year and 5-year yields each declined 7.2 basis points, while the 10-year fell 3.7 basis points to 5.163%. The 30-year rose 1.5 basis points to 5.494% after reaching 5.53% during trading. Some investors unwound earlier curve-flattening positions as the front end already reflected substantial tightening.

The economic releases did not resolve the inflation concern. September consumer sentiment beat expectations but weakened from August, while year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.6% from 4%. Durable-goods orders were effectively unchanged, better than expected, but growth excluding transportation disappointed. Lower real yields accounted for the 10-year nominal yield's decline; inflation compensation increased.

U.S. investment-grade, high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads all widened noticeably. Weekly U.S. corporate issuance fell short of expectations, and Prospect Capital's proposed refinancing near 8% illustrated the cost of replacing much cheaper debt. Japan's firmer underlying inflation and coordinated official support for the yen added to the broader pressure for tighter policy. Friday's oil retreat remained dependent on negotiations that had yet to produce an agreement.
overall_summary.summary: Hopes for a Hormuz agreement eased energy pressure, but rising household inflation expectations and concerns about government financing and further Fed tightening kept the recovery concentrated in shorter maturities.
